title: Tenant SLO shaper + phase coordinator for latency-first scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware SLO shaper and phase coordinator that dynamically fuses or splits prefill/decode phases to meet per-tenant latency SLOs while reducing unfair starvation and preserving aggregate throughput. The shaper should: 1) consume per-tenant latency windows and priority weights, 2) select phase fusion vs split based on predicted kernel cost and KV cache hit profiles, and 3) emit control signals to the prefiller/decoder arbiter for microbatch sizing and hedged execution. This ticket covers spec, simulator validation, initial implementation behind a feature flag, and a staged rollout with telemetry and automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end feature behind runtime flag that can be toggled per-cluster
99th percentile latency for P0 tenants improves by at least 18% on tail-heavy traces compared to baseline without >5% throughput regression
Fairness (normalized completion time across tenants at equal weight) improves or remains within 5% of baseline under mixed workloads
Canary rollout to a single region with automated rollback on error rate increase >1% or latency regression >10%
Unit + integration tests for phase decision logic and simulation harness included
Observability: dashboards for per-tenant SLO compliance, decision logs, kernel selection events, and cache-hit correlations
implementation_notes: Decision input vector: tenant SLO target, recent tail-latency histogram, queue depth, kernel-cost estimate, KV cache hit probability, and tenant weight
Phase fusion heuristic favors fusion when estimated decode kernel cost is dominated by prefill KV transfer and when KV hit rate > threshold
Use lightweight ML model (gradient-boosted tree) trained on perf traces to predict latency delta of fusion vs split; initial model shipped as config table with simulated-safe defaults
Expose tuning knobs in Console: per-tenant latency target override, aggressive/ conservative mode, and max microbatch size
Backpressure: if downstream queue depth exceeds N, automatically favor split to reduce head-of-line blocking
Fallbacks: fallback to current fairshare scheduler if model confidence low or kernel probe errors occur
